thread.title: FAANG Stocks Set to Rebound as AMD Plunges

author: investopedia.com
title: FAANG Stocks Set to Rebound as AMD Plunges
text:
U.S. equity futures pointed higher on Thursday morning after Wednesday's bloodbath, and it seems investors aren’t quite ready to quit FAANG stocks just yet.
All five members of the group rebounded slightly after markets closed yesterday. In pre-market trading , Facebook Inc. ( FB ), Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ), Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) and Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) Google’s share prices were all up around 2%. The tech-focused Nasdaq rose 1.5% in the early hours of Thursday after having its worst day since August 2011. The NYSE FANG+ Index, which tracks the so-called FAANG stocks, together with the likes of Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ), Twitter Inc. ( TWTR ), Alibaba ( BABA ) and Baidu ( BIDU ), fell 5.39% yesterday to $2,430, down 20% from its record high close on June 20.
A decent run after the closing bell suggests that some investors now think FAANG stocks have been excessively punished, following another grueling session for the big tech stocks and the rest of the equity market on Wednesday.
On tap today are the latest earnings reports from several big tech firms, including Twitter, Alphabet, Amazon, Snap and Intel. Tesla and Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ) shares were higher after the companies beat Wall Street expectations.
Semiconductor Stocks Continue to Fall Out of Favor Signs that appetite for big tech stocks, which were mainly responsible for propelling the S&P 500 Index (SPX) and other major market barometers upward in recent years, could be returning did not extend to large semiconductor companies.
The share prices of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. ( AMD ) and Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) plunged 18.03% and 0.80% in pre-market trading, suggesting that the chipmaking heavyweights both could be in for another difficult day. Micron Technology Inc. ( MU ), meanwhile, edged up 0.34%, having shed 8.40% on Wednesday.
Sentiment in semiconductor stocks has plummeted, amid an escalation of the U.S.-China trade war and concerns around China's economic growth. The VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ) ended Wednesday down 6.7%, its biggest fall since November 2008, after Nvidia’s shares got hammered, AMD fell off disappointing third-quarter revenues and Texas Instruments Inc. ( TXN ) reduced its guidance and posted lower than expected quarterly earnings.
Matt Maley, equity strategist at Miller Tabak, told CNBC that the semiconductor sell-off is justified as “super-high valuations” fall out of sync with slowing demand.
"What concerns us is most of the companies in the index are trading at super-high valuations, you may see demand slowing, and the perception is such that with these trade and tariff wars, with everything going on in China and across the U.S., that people are concerned with how this settles out," he said.
